_metadata.purpose: Complete database inventory for Papers 1 and 2 with raw and deduplicated counts

pleiades.note: No deduplication needed; each entry is a unique place

p3k14c.raw_entries_note: 173,946 radiocarbon dates from Bird et al. 2022 (180,070 total; 173,946 after cleaning)
p3k14c.dates_after_coord_filter_note: 170,150 retained after filtering for valid coordinates
p3k14c.deduplicated_sites_note: 36,693 unique SiteID-deduplicated sites; 25,557 in the upgraded Z computation (different dedup method)

dare.note: Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire; each entry is a unique place

peru_ministry.note: Peru Ministry of Culture geoportal; georeferenced archaeological sites

saaid.note: South American Archaeological Isotopic Database v2.0; unique sites

historic_england.note: Negative control database; circle does not pass within 50 km of UK

luwian_site_atlas.note: Bronze Age western Anatolia (2000-1200 BCE); null result (0/483 within 500 km)

total_A_deduplicated_unique_sites.note: Sum of deduplicated unique sites across all 10 databases (using 36,693 for p3k14c SiteID dedup)

total_B_raw_entries_for_radiocarbon_dbs.note: Treating p3k14c as 173,946 raw dates and XRONOS as 305,400 raw records; first 5 databases only

which_supports_550k_claim.explanation: The '550,000 entries' claim in Paper 2 counts raw database entries/dates, not deduplicated sites. The 5-database raw sum is 605,489, making 550K an undercount. The deduplicated site total is only ~259K, which does not support the 550K figure.
which_supports_550k_claim.recommendation: Say 'over 550,000 database entries' or '~259,000 unique archaeological sites'. Never say '550,000 sites'.
